subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should hook-agent deliveries with an already-active resolved sessionKey be rejected with 409, queued, serialized, or left parallel by default?
rationale: The requested behavior changes an external webhook HTTP contract and overlaps with persistent-session and queued-webhook designs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API policy.

options.title: Add Explicit 409 Guard
options.body: Reject direct and mapped hook-agent deliveries when the resolved sessionKey is active, ideally behind a deliberate hook or mapping policy so existing callers keep current behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Queued Webhooks
options.body: Let queued webhook ingestion own overlap control, backlog visibility, and per-queue parallelism instead of making immediate POSTs fail.

options.title: Keep Caller-Owned Locking
options.body: Leave immediate hooks parallel and document that integrations should use idempotency keys, queues, or external locks until a broader design lands.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit 409 Guard
recommendation.body: Reject direct and mapped hook-agent deliveries when the resolved sessionKey is active, ideally behind a deliberate hook or mapping policy so existing callers keep current behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is product/API policy across Gateway hook ingress and session-state safety, and Peter has prior routing signal in the related cleanup discussion.
